Owned arithmetic sumcheck polynomials retain their original compact coefficients and unused field tails after binding. Release those working copies after their callers have moved to bound coefficients and final claims. Original committed polynomials remain available for the PCS.

## Topic, type and dependencies

- **Topic:** prover memory and ownership.
- **Type:** allocation and retained-memory optimization. Test portability is separate below. This does not add or weaken a proof relation.
- **Base:** `perf/native-arithmetic-prerequisites` at `04cb07d002b33780f46ae7f269fb032bcc4ed840`, a prerequisite-only merge of #350 and #362. The topic group does not change merge order.
- **Candidate:** `b2b6459fca5ca3e09132c91e2009f60a8a844692`.

## Implementation

The audited multiplication, addition, contraction, reduction, clamp, reciprocal, square-root, maximum and hidden-read provers reuse the opening reclamation helper after binding. It converts only owned working copies to the remaining field polynomial, then reclaims sufficiently large unused tails geometrically. There are 20 calls across nine arithmetic modules. Generic binding and cloning, range proof state and identity polynomials keep their existing behavior.

The less-than polynomial tests use the configured challenge alias so the full-field configuration compiles. This is test portability; its production arithmetic is unchanged. The independent references check complete round messages, remaining coefficients, original evaluations and final opening claims, including permitted integer extrema and literal zero/one in the full-field configuration.

## Measurements and limits

These are complete native inference and receipt comparisons, not ordinary Atlas inference or outer recursion. Both sides include all required source, conversion, hidden-boundary and solver checks. Each native comparison has one sequential sample per source on its original host. The second candidate also has finer commitment tracing, so it does not isolate instrumentation overhead.

| Scope | Control | Reclamation | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Policy process peak, Xeon Platinum 8272L, 48 workers | 163.36 GiB | 140.88 GiB | −22.48 GiB, −13.8% |
| Policy commitments and proving | 1,288.84 s | 1,286.98 s | −1.86 s, essentially unchanged |
| Planner process peak, Xeon E7-8890 v4, 32 workers | 162.98 GiB | 140.26 GiB | −22.72 GiB, −13.9% |
| Planner commitments and proving | 1,676.97 s | 1,710.55 s | +33.58 s, +2.0% |
| Planner whole native command | 3,060.88 s | 3,083.24 s | +22.36 s, +0.7% |

This is a measured memory saving with time tradeoffs, not a proving-speed claim. The isolated allocation fixture retains the originals: working capacity falls from 640 to 512 MiB, while binding slows from 0.109 to 0.176 seconds. It uses 16 workers and two samples per mode in control, candidate, candidate, control order. Capacity and whole-process RSS are distinct quantities. No proof-size or verifier optimization is introduced, and no general repeatability claim is made.

The policy control is the authenticated arithmetic-profile source; its candidate adds the focused reclamation. The planner control is the accepted integrated source at `cc299bc`, and its candidate is `9993f20`, which adds reclamation and timing attribution. This PR contains the generic reclamation and tests, not the application tracing wrapper.

## Validation

- Exact upstream source passes **308 ZK and 169 ordinary library tests**, both independent reference tests with production and full-field challenges, formatting and strict ordinary/ZK library Clippy on Linux with Rust 1.97.1 and debug assertions enabled for tests.
- The full-field configuration retains two unused-import warnings in unchanged field code; strict full-field Clippy is not claimed.
- Application integration passes **334 ZK, 191 ordinary and five driver tests**, 19 action/receiver/sampler tests and strict library/driver Clippy.
- Both complete native receipts pass required consumers and boundaries. The fresh planner also passes all 36 receipt substitution controls, 14 malformed-message controls, receiver reservation/replay/stale-state checks and relocated public verification.
- Archives authenticate. Exact upstream validation retains 462 pinned files, including three Python bytecode caches. The complete receipt archive intentionally omits only those three caches and authenticates all 459 remaining source files. Every compiled source matches. Dedicated Linux checks and GitHub CI are separate.

[Exact upstream validation](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/c0783d6/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-19-native-arithmetic-storage), [complete policy comparison](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/6207280/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-19-policy-arithmetic-candidate), and [complete planner comparison and Perfetto traces](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/c0783d6/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-19-action-arithmetic).

## Repository CI comparison

The September 20 observation records five passing GitHub jobs: formatting, default Clippy/tests, GPT-2, BGE and Wasm. The workspace ZK job fails. Running that command with the repository's Rust 1.95.0 on exact base `04cb07d` and candidate `b2b6459` reproduces the same error messages and source locations as GitHub. The failures concern missing activation-table constants, unused imports and unused softmax cache methods. No workflow or proof check is relaxed.

## Topic, type and dependencies

- **Topic:** prover memory and ownership.
- **Type:** retained-storage optimization and the associated public API migration. This does not add or weaken a proof relation.
- **Base:** #288, `perf/round-2` at `cfcffb05dcc76599f4e5b3d01c6e13f5fa653e13`.
- **Head:** `7455985239ac1f6629a21eb5de51c67aca973dba`. The additional fully populated representation extends `593fc22c8fef3bd1a3bd3c933a4c903ea70169f6`.
- Related memory work is in #349, #353, #354, #357, #358 and #362. The topic group does not change merge order. The complete policy comparison below includes #362 on both sides.

## Representation and unchanged relations

Vectors with absent entries reserve code zero for absence. Tables below 256 entries use bytes, and tables below 65,536 entries use shorts. Fully populated tables of exactly 256 or 65,536 entries need no absence code and can use one or two bytes respectively. Short vectors retain direct storage when the decoding table would erase the saving. Every address is checked before encoding, including values after an absent entry. Explicit fresh allocations avoid retaining the wider input buffer.

`OneHotPolynomial::from_indices` still accepts the same vector. Its `nonzero_indices` field exposes immutable views, so users of Vec-specific methods must migrate to those views. The additional representation needs no further API change. Encoding choice is internal and is not serialized. Proof messages, transcript operations, original committed polynomials, independent commitment blinding and verifier predicates remain unchanged. Constant-time or oblivious-memory execution is not established.

## Complete policy comparison for compact optional addresses

This comparison measures the integrated compact-index source at `593fc22`, before the additional fully populated representation. The control uses four-byte optional addresses with opening-buffer reclamation. Both sides use the original Xeon Platinum 8272L and 48 native workers, with one completed sample per source.

| Original index allocation | 69.97 GiB | 33.29 GiB | −36.68 GiB |
| Native proof body | 250,283 bytes | 250,283 bytes | unchanged |

Original registration, both hidden tensor boundaries, required consumers and every receipt and malformed-message control pass. Archives authenticate, and process and Rust Perfetto traces import without errors or unfinished spans. These single samples show a memory saving with time regressions. They establish neither a proving-speed gain nor general repeatability.

## Complete action comparison for fully populated addresses

The additional representation at `7455985` is integrated into a complete native
action receipt. The benchmark baseline is accepted application source `c0783d6`,
which already includes compact optional addresses and arithmetic reclamation.
The only Rust change in the candidate is `compact_indices.rs`; two Cargo paths
select the isolated build. Both use the original Xeon E7-8890 v4, 32 native
workers, 16 consumer workers, the same model, original registered setup, numerical
fixture and fine tracing. There is one sequential complete sample per source.

small encoded-length differences. This storage change is not a proof-size
optimization. One current full-validation observation is
54.82 seconds, including internal rejection
trials; it is not a matched verifier-speed comparison.

All original numerical and committed-witness checks, native graph and hidden
boundaries, fresh required consumers and both solver queries, 36 receipt and
14 malformed-message controls, receiver reservation/replay/stale-state checks
and relocated verification pass. Original model, native registration and cached
policy proof bytes remain fixed. Both archives and every compiled source file
authenticate. Complete Rust and process traces import without errors, and the
rental is collected and stopped. These single samples establish no general
repeatability or tenfold proving claim. The policy comparison above and isolated
fixtures below retain their separate sources and scopes.

[Complete action source and results](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/9d884f21d547e19ee15fbd67642d9ac85904aa57/native-atlas/application-action-present-indices),
[authenticated complete receipt and comparison](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/9d884f21d547e19ee15fbd67642d9ac85904aa57/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-20-action-present-indices).

All **483 application files** reproduce exactly. Strict application library Clippy passes. The full-field configuration retains two warnings in unchanged field imports and has no strict Clippy claim.

Workspace ZK fails with the same 50 normalized errors and source locations as independently executed exact base `cfcffb05` and previous head `593fc22`. [Exact CI comparison](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/9d884f21d547e19ee15fbd67642d9ac85904aa57/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-20-action-present-indices/upstream-ci).

Sparse lookup commitments can spend most row-addition work on one frequent address. This update keeps bounded row segments and recovers a frequent row from a cached sum of the public generators. Every commitment row and opening hint remains in its original position.

## Topic and dependencies

- **Topic:** prover computation, commitments and scheduling.
- **Type:** performance optimization. The reference tests establish equivalence; this is not a proof-soundness repair.
- **Base:** #336, `feat/native-first-maximum`, reviewed base `bc75d22ff010`. The series starts from `perf/round-2`.
- **Current follow-up:** `59fe05a99607b1252b2baa35530805b927497a80` extends this PR's `fc57b41f19f15a6ea5f02234ec79a316235fda1f`. The branch dependency is unchanged.

## Bounded row segments

Each aligned column segment groups its indices by address, applies the existing batched affine row sum and writes the result in the original row order. Temporary point storage is bounded by the running segments rather than the entire polynomial. Segments use the existing Rayon pool.

The preceding public-setup comparison remains separate. For 2^22 indices and eight workers, two reversed-order pairs average **3.883 → 2.252 s**, a reduction of **1.631 s (42.00%, 1.724×)**. Process peak including setup decode averages **1.145 → 0.716 GiB**, a reduction of **0.429 GiB (37.47%)**. Public commitments are byte-identical. This is a kernel measurement, not a full-model result, and its baseline is the unsegmented configuration described in the original experiment.

## Cached public sums

A complete aligned segment partitions the column generators among its address rows. Their total is fixed by the public setup. If one row contains at least half the entries and at least 32 entries, compute the remaining rows and subtract them from that total. Incomplete segments, short vectors and insufficiently skewed inputs use the established path.

The lazy cache belongs to the exact setup and power-of-two column width. It contains only public generator sums, is absent from serialized setup bytes and is empty after deserialization. Its initializer is sequential to avoid reentrant Rayon work under an initialization lock. Row construction remains parallel. Commitment equations, every row and hint, independent fresh hiding masks, transcript order and proof format are unchanged.

### Isolated comparison for this update

The benchmark control is the exact accepted segmented row kernel in application code `9d884f2`, frozen in a test module. Both modes use the same binary and immutable compact input view. The generic branch uses ordinary slices; production row code and the setup constructor match the application after only that input-type normalization. Source recipes and the exact comparison are in [the implementation package](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/dddfe49193cf907fff215446d155cf872e4e3889/native-atlas/application-action-sparse-rows) and [authenticated evidence](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/dddfe49193cf907fff215446d155cf872e4e3889/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-20-sparse-rows-kernel).

The skewed input assigns at least seven eighths to one address; the missing input omits every seventeenth position. Each distribution runs control, candidate, candidate, control in separate processes, with one cold and one warm call per process. There are two samples per mode, compilation is excluded, and all serialized rows match exactly.

## Topic and evidence summary

**Review group:** Proof transport and shared commitments. **Type:** Performance + decoder hardening.

Compress ordinary HyperKZG advice, identifiers and exact repeated coefficients; bound decoding and restore original canonical transcript bytes.

**Baseline and observed effect.** Complete ordinary Qwen inner proof: 5,188,295 → 2,941,543 bytes; 2,246,752 bytes less (43.30% reduction; 1.764× baseline/candidate). Prepared input: 6,535,393 → 4,288,657 bytes. Matched canonical/v2 guest cycles: 1,940,734,622 → 1,906,064,251 (1.79% fewer). Compared with v1, v2 saves 7.51% proof bytes but costs 0.062% more cycles; all pad to 2^31 rows. No measured outer proving or peak-memory gain. Malformed/canonicality checks harden the new format; this does not imply the old canonical format was unsound.

**Dependencies.** This PR targets #288 (`perf/round-2`); reviewed head `b80c74bf533d`, code base `cfcffb05dcc7`. The benchmark baseline is the configuration described above and below, which may include other integrated changes. The topic group does not change merge order. Related PRs: #343.

<!-- atlas-topic-review:2026-09-19:end -->

Ordinary BN254/HyperKZG proofs repeat softmax identifiers, small advice values, and reduction coefficients. This adds an opt-in compact format with bounded direct decoding and exact recovery of the canonical proof bytes, including streaming those bytes into an existing transcript hash. The recorded complete Qwen proof shrinks from 5,188,295 to 2,941,543 bytes (43.30%).

The format stores contiguous softmax u32 advice in runs, shares ordinary identifier prefixes, and references exact one-coefficient reductions already present in opening claims. Decoding reconstructs every original claim and coefficient before normal verification. It rejects invalid scalar/point encodings, oversized collections, duplicate or unordered keys, nonmaximal prefixes/runs, alternative literal/reference forms, overflow, truncation and trailing bytes. Existing canonical serialization is unchanged. Native ZK and Dory formats are outside this API's scope.

`deserialize_compact_with_canonical` streams the original canonical bytes without expanding a full proof buffer. The decoder reuses original scalar bytes for reduction references and validated polynomial identifiers for preserved prefixes. On targets narrower than u64, identifiers are round-tripped to reject index narrowing; field and curve validation remain on all targets. `compact-format.md` documents the `ATLSCP02` layout and the native conversion benchmark. Version 2 supersedes this PR's experimental version-1 marker.

### Matched complete-input measurements

All three guests below include the same separately validated verifier-computation patch in the zkARc integration. That computation change is separate from this PR; these columns isolate the encoding choice. The saved Qwen2-0.5B proof, constant proof, statement, numerical outputs and complete verification relation are unchanged.

| Complete Qwen | Canonical control | Compact v1 (`1555b98`) | Compact v2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Compressed inner proof, bytes | 5,188,295 | 3,180,228 | 2,941,543 |
| Prepared verifier input, bytes | 6,535,393 | 4,527,342 | 4,288,657 |
| Actual complete guest cycles | 1,940,734,622 | 1,904,887,318 | 1,906,064,251 |
| Padded trace rows | 2^31 | 2^31 | 2^31 |

Version 2 saves another 238,685 bytes (7.51%) versus version 1: 150,626 from identifiers and 88,059 from reduction references. It costs 0.062% more guest cycles than version 1, while using 1.79% fewer than the matched canonical control. This is an opt-in storage/execution tradeoff; it does not replace the faster codec in the queued outer-proof experiments. No new outer proof, proving-time improvement or peak-memory saving is claimed.

The Add/ReLU control, without softmax, shrinks from 15,332 to 14,503 proof bytes and from 20,880 to 20,067 prepared-input bytes. Its canonical/v1/v2 guests use 75,468,879 / 75,419,492 / 75,443,291 cycles. Each input passes native and frozen independent verification, exact independent Python byte recovery, changed-statement/IO/constant/advice/sumcheck rejection, and individual missing-deferred-proof rejection. Additional checks reject changed reduction coefficients and missing reductions, including coefficients bound by the constant transcript but ignored by the single-consumer shortcut.

Receipts, frozen sources and rejected decoder trials are retained in zkARc's `bench-logs/2026-09-17-atlas-compact-v2/`; `compare.py` checks artifacts, source hashes and the measurements. Canonical Qwen proof SHA-256: `c946286339b7e499c0e1351135b4bdde359bf415a22536b251a519a4b9dd983e`. Version-2 proof SHA-256: `ea455865a2b10096d9b37d13f5b9a1499d99dcda3e7b2cf8799db721922eb35f`.

- Eight codec tests pass, covering both compression modes, complete softmax proving/verification, malformed records, full-width identifiers, exact legacy streaming and writer failure.
- The existing complete transformer serialization/verification test passes.
- Strict all-target core Clippy, workspace formatting, and eight integration guest-library tests pass.
- Both complete prepared inputs pass native verification, the independent verifier and rejection controls; six actual guest executions cover canonical/v1/v2 controls and candidates.
- The native example checks exact round trips and reports ten alternating decode samples per format. Native timings are shared-host decoding only, not proving measurements.

cargo test --locked --profile build-fast -p jolt-atlas-core proof_serialization::tests

cargo fmt --all --check

## Summary

Reshape verification constructs a selector table with one entry per padded tensor element, then evaluates that table at the input opening point. When every input and output dimension is a power of two, flat indices are unchanged. The selector evaluation is exactly the equality polynomial at the two opening points.

Evaluate that formula directly in both ordinary verification and the ZK challenge-value calculation. Keep the existing table path for shapes requiring padding. Check the tensor domain and opening-point lengths before taking the direct path. The prover, coefficients, transcript and proof encoding are unchanged.

## Validation

`cargo test --release -p jolt-atlas-core --lib onnx_proof::ops::reshape::tests` passes all four tests with the recorded local arkworks compatibility patches.

- Compare the direct result against the original materialized table on seven shape pairs, random and Boolean points, singleton dimensions, an empty opening point for a one-element tensor, and shapes with internal padding.
- Reject an opening point of the wrong dimension even when both supplied point lengths agree.
- Existing complete proof tests pass for four unpadded shape pairs and the padded `[10, 10]` to `[20, 5]` reshape.

The recorded corrected Qwen proof has 195 reshapes, all with dimensions that are powers of two. The complete guest accepts in 36,241,922,278 cycles, compared with 42,618,879,428 before this change (14.96% fewer). Both runs use the same prepared witness and already include PRs #295 and #296 and Jolt Blake2 compression. All eight native rejection controls pass. This remains above the configured outer proving bound, and no Qwen outer proof is claimed.

## CI scope

Native/default tests, GPT-2, BGE, formatting and WASM checks pass. The native ZK job fails at unchanged division and lookup API imports, also present on the other branches from this base. The direct selector formula is shared with ZK challenge calculation, but a complete native ZK regression is not established by this PR. Broader Qwen ZK coverage is tracked in #289.

## Summary

`HyperKZG::combine_commitments` currently computes each scalar multiplication separately and then sums the results. A measured current Qwen proof contains 18,154 commitments, making this expensive inside a verifier guest.

Use the existing `msm_field_elements` routine to compute the same linear combination in one MSM (a sum of points multiplied by scalar coefficients). This retains the points, coefficients, transcript and proof encoding. Mismatched lengths fail explicitly instead of silently truncating through `zip`.

- Complete prepared-verifier regressions pass with the change, including malformed encodings, changed commitments, claims and execution IO.

- Added direct equality regressions against separate scalar multiplications for empty and mixed batches, repeated/opposite/identity points, and zero, unit, negative and random coefficients. A separate regression checks coefficient length mismatch.

The fixture now has a complete outer Jolt proof of 97,814 bytes, separately measured verifier preprocessing of 67,347 bytes and 160 bytes of public IO. Fresh verification accepts, rejects a changed statement/result, and confirms private advice is absent from serialized IO. Proving took 394.48 seconds after 441.02 seconds of fresh setup on the EPYC 7B13 with 32 Rayon threads. This is one measurement with other traces running, not a controlled timing comparison.

The complete corrected Qwen guest now accepts in 42,719,182,959 cycles, compared with 61,320,942,771 with inline Blake2 before the MSM change, a 30.3% reduction on the same saved witness. Both counts remain above the current guest proving bound. No Qwen outer proof is claimed.

## Topic and evidence summary

**Review group:** Correctness and verifier portability. **Type:** Bug fix.

Preserve real-element order when reshape dimensions are padded; lower affected cases through existing checked operators.

**Baseline and observed effect.** No timing or memory gain claimed. Qwen last-logit cosine on one prompt: 0.931922 → 0.999874, with the reference next token and top ten restored. This is numerical correctness evidence, not translation accuracy or a proving-speed comparison; the registered imported graph changes.

**Dependencies.** This PR targets #288 (`perf/round-2`); reviewed head `a78b7a5c83ae`, code base `29170bd3a813`. The benchmark baseline is the configuration described above and below, which may include other integrated changes. The topic group does not change merge order. Related PRs: #292, #294, #335.

<!-- atlas-topic-review:2026-09-19:end -->

## Problem and change

Padding each reshape dimension independently can change logical element order. For example, `[2, 3, 4] -> [6, 4]` becomes `[2, 4, 4] -> [8, 4]`; the fourth row of the first group is padding, so a flat reshape shifts the second group's data. The same issue misaligns Qwen2-0.5B's 14 query heads with its two groups of seven shared-key heads.

Detect reshapes that move real elements under padding and lower them to existing reshape, gather, broadcast and multiplication operators. A common trailing shape stays together, so attention gathers entire blocks instead of individual scalars. A mask clears newly introduced padding. Compatible reshapes retain their existing path. Update input/output identities and original-weight shadow mappings after inserting nodes. This changes the imported graph and its registered model identity; it adds no proof operator or unchecked verifier shortcut.

## Validation

- Eight reshape cases cover merging, splitting, non-power-of-two trailing dimensions, unequal padded element counts and the actual Qwen attention shapes. Compatible layouts remain unchanged.
- Three small ONNX fixtures pass imported forward and original-weight shadow checks.
- Complete ordinary Atlas proofs for those three imported fixtures verify and reject an altered output. Serialized proofs are 4,734, 4,734 and 5,206 bytes. These are correctness fixtures with test setup.
- The unchanged Qwen2-0.5B export, scale 14, sequence length 32, on one recorded prompt now selects the original ONNX Runtime next token (20728), with top-ten overlap 10/10. Last-logit cosine improves from 0.931922 to 0.999874 and mean absolute error is 0.0518575.
- The original-weight floating shadow after the correction matches the original ONNX reference with mean absolute error 0.00000289 and top-ten overlap 10/10, the same result as disabling padding.

The Qwen comparison retains only the final vocabulary projection after all transformer layers. A separate equality check confirms that this projection rewrite preserves every final logit. These are numerical checks on one prompt, not a translation-accuracy or full Qwen proof claim. Attention-mask headroom is tracked separately in #292. The Qwen proof measurement will use both changes.

Local builds use Rust 1.97.1, the pinned Tract revision `c484b3ee9a22e7d2bfca8394619771397b61c0d6`, and the same arkworks compatibility export used for the paper experiments. CI's native ZK module has existing API mismatches also seen on the other isolated branches; this change does not repair that module.

## Topic and evidence summary

**Review group:** Correctness and verifier portability. **Type:** Bug fix.

Restore additive-mask headroom: a masked score must not win merely because the sentinel was derived only from the exponential cutoff. The finite-mask condition and integer range still apply.

**Baseline and observed effect.** No performance optimization claimed. Correctness baseline: scores [0,20] plus the old -12 mask become [0,8], allowing the masked position to win; the regression checks zero probability at masked positions with restored headroom. Quantized models and registrations must be regenerated.

**Dependencies.** This PR targets #288 (`perf/round-2`); reviewed head `286e433558db`, code base `29170bd3a813`. The benchmark baseline is the configuration described above and below, which may include other integrated changes. The topic group does not change merge order. Related PRs: #293, #294, #335.

<!-- atlas-topic-review:2026-09-19:end -->

## Problem and change

The small attention-mask sentinel is chosen only from the exponential table's cutoff. That does not make it a valid additive mask for arbitrary attention scores. At scale 14, scores `[0, 20]` with the second position masked become `[0, 8]` after adding the current `-12` sentinel. The masked position wins.

Restore the earlier `-2^30` integer headroom for extreme negative mask constants. Correct the documentation to state the actual finite-mask condition: its magnitude must exceed the score difference plus the exponential cutoff, and the addition must stay in range. This is still a finite approximation to negative infinity, not an unconditional guarantee for all representable scores.

Add a regression with a larger masked score and an Atlas proof regression that adds the mask before softmax. Update the older attention fixture to use the restored sentinel. The current generic significance clamp already handles the larger gap.

## Validation

- A standalone native proof harness constructs two attention rows with one unmasked score of zero and seven masked scores of twenty. The resulting mask/add/softmax graph assigns zero probability to every masked position.
- Its complete ordinary HyperKZG proof verifies, and a changed output is rejected. The proof serializes to 26,445 bytes. This uses Atlas test setup for a correctness regression.
- A full Qwen2-0.5B forward pass completes with the change. It still disagrees with the floating-point reference on the recorded prompt's next token, so this PR does not claim to resolve Qwen's broader quantization error.

The native proof build uses pinned Tract and the existing arkworks compatibility export. Cached quantized models and their registrations need regeneration because the affected constant values change.

Native BlindFold verification currently retains stage relations, batched constraint copies and challenge vectors used only for witness construction. It also clones builder inputs and keeps every intermediate constraint row alive while producing the sparse matrices. This change consumes those values and releases them after their final use. A distinct verifier wrapper exposes only verification; the prover constructor keeps its witness-building data.

**Topic:** native verifier. **Type:** performance optimization through ownership and storage lifetimes. No protocol or acceptance-predicate change is intended.

**Base and dependencies:** this PR is stacked directly on #359 (`perf/ordered-opening-deduplication`, `bbcc441a6ae6a2ebec3055275a155c5fb5a1707c`), which is stacked on #355 (Dory target-group MSM). Topic labels do not change that merge order. The final head is `3deadf84856bf127c39e011ce5c2da88b2229cca`. Its production source is byte-identical to measured head `4c60effc0e22a8f165845364062eab37f4f7f02f`; the final commit only replaces three temporary cloned slices in the new tests with borrowed slices.

### Changes

- `NativeBlindFold::new_verifier` uses the same assembly and validation logic, consumes each stage, and omits witness-only retained copies. The existing prover constructor and borrowed builder APIs remain available.
- The owned R1CS builder moves configurations and public coefficients through construction. It consumes intermediate rows while appending the same sparse matrix entries in the same order.
- Native graph verification releases its first-stage operator verifiers after sumcheck has recorded their owned relations and openings.

Matrix coefficients, row and variable ordering, aliases, repeated-opening constraints, commitment layout, external evaluation count, transcript order and proof encoding remain unchanged. The test oracle contains the original assembly and original builder rather than comparing two paths through the new implementation.

### Measured application scope

| Complete saved-receipt scope | Baseline | Candidate | Absolute reduction | Relative reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean process maximum RSS | 1.4848 GiB | 0.9876 GiB | 0.4972 GiB | 33.49% |
| Mean honest verification after decoding | 60.919 s | 60.232 s | 0.686 s | 1.13% |
| Mean whole verification command | 61.195 s | 60.455 s | 0.740 s | 1.21% |

All four timed honest checks accept. This is an observed host-memory improvement; verification time remains approximately one minute.

The code base above differs from the application benchmark baseline: the latter is the pinned zkARc complete-verifier export with the existing fixed registered parameters, exact membership certificates, batched decoder, in-place transcript reversal and allocator-reuse integration. The before/after source maps and binary/input hashes identify both builds. Only this storage patch differs in production source. Both verify the same saved complete receipt, including both native graphs, hidden tensor boundaries, required Jolt consumers, solver queries and receiver bindings.

Linux x86_64, Xeon E5-2640 v4, 20 exposed logical CPUs, Rust 1.97.1, release build with `host`, `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8`. Two observations per variant, sequential ABBA order, independently built target directories. Honest verification time starts after input decoding; command time and maximum RSS cover the whole process. These are observations on one host, without an established general repeatability claim. No new proof was generated. Guest cycles, fixed-arena memory capacity, native proving and outer proving are unmeasured for this candidate. The previous complete guest exceeded its selected trace capacity and later exhausted its arena; this host result does not establish that either limit is resolved.

### Validation

- Measured upstream source: 311 ZK library tests passed, 2 benchmark tests ignored, using the normal test profile and one test thread; strict ZK library Clippy passed.
- All three added differential tests passed again on the final head, along with strict library lint. They compare complete matrices/layouts at multiple widths and sizes, repeats, aliases, empty/uniskip/chained configurations, nonlinear relations and input scaling; malformed shapes retain their rejection behavior. They also check that the verifier retains no witness-only vectors.
- Application source: 12 complete-verifier tests and strict package-only Clippy passed. The complete honest receipt accepts and all 44 actual substitutions reject.
- Source reproduction and committed upstream identity are audited independently of acceptance results.

The initial parallel release suite had three setup-cache read failures and two guardrail tests expecting debug assertions disabled by that profile. Those failed logs are retained; the accepted run uses the existing normal test profile, a fresh setup cache and serial test execution. No verification check was relaxed. Dependency-wide strict application lint still reports the same 21 findings and locations on the exact unchanged control; package-only and upstream strict checks above pass. An initial benchmark never executed after copied binaries lost executable permissions; its shared target also produced identical binaries. That attempt is excluded. Accepted measurements use distinct executables from separate target directories.

Additional ZK test-target Clippy retains two findings reproduced on exact base `bbcc441`; the new tests have no remaining findings. One diagnostic line shifts with the inserted production line, and that diagnostic source line is checked identical.

**Repository CI, observed 2026-09-21 16:16 UTC on final head `3deadf8`:** format, default Clippy/tests, GPT-2, BGE and WebAssembly jobs pass. The ZK CI job reports the same six errors and source locations as the exact unchanged base. The linked evidence includes both job logs and the normalized comparison; this PR does not claim a passing ZK CI job.

Evidence and reproduction: [measured report and reproduction](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/4205b03c1729e079b95e1c998d478ddc5482ecbe/native-atlas/blindfold-verifier-storage/results.md). Source-equivalence explanation: [relation preservation](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/4205b03c1729e079b95e1c998d478ddc5482ecbe/native-atlas/blindfold-verifier-storage/equivalence.md). The public evidence contains source/input/executable hashes and selected logs; original receipt inputs and large archives remain in the preserved local experiment bundle.
